newsitem.title: USA: Fed adds temporary reserves via 14-day system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed adds temporary reserves via 14-day system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve added temporary reserves to the banking system on Thursday through 14-day fixed system repurchase agreements, a Fed spokeswoman confirmed.
Federal funds were trading at 5-1/4 percent, the Fed's target for the rate, at the time of the operation.
Analysts had predicted a temporary reserve addition, saying a 14-day operation was a possibility.
The Fed has a growing seasonal add need, analysts said.

Patricia Thrapp, vice president at Aubrey G. Lanston & Co., estimated an average daily add need for the Fed at $8.0 billion in the first part of the two-week bank reserve maintenance period and an average daily add need of $10.5 billion in the second part of the period.

A rise in currency in circulation over the coming Presidents Day holiday weekend and settlement of the Treasury's $39.75 billion quarterly refinancing on Tuesday, February 18, would contribute to the pressure on bank reserves, making a reserve addition necessary, she said.
((-- E. Freilich, North American Treasury Desk 212-859-1679))
